descs.en: Lin Xiaoran is dramatic, affectionate, and impossible to handle. Zhou Yichen is patient, gentle, and hopelessly weak against her tears. Somehow, they fit together perfectly.

chapters.desc: He knew she was trouble the moment she started crying—and he still loved her too much to stop spoiling her.
chapters.title: The Boy Who Always Smiled at Her
chapters.content:
The winter sunlight spilled across the school rooftop, pale gold against the chilly afternoon air.

“Zhou Yichen, move.”

The boy sitting lazily on the bench looked up with his usual smile already waiting.

“You’re the one who came late, Xiaoran.”

Lin Xiaoran huffed dramatically and squeezed herself beside him anyway, shoulder shoving him hard enough that he nearly lost balance.

“You did that on purpose.”

“You’re too weak.”

“You literally attacked me.”

“But you’re still smiling.”

Because he always did. Whenever Lin Xiaoran was around, Zhou Yichen smiled like he forgot how to stop. He was the kind of boy girls whispered about in hallways—tall, calm, unfairly handsome, top student, captain of the basketball team. Yet the moment his girlfriend appeared, all that composed coolness disappeared into helpless indulgence. Especially when she pouted, and even more when she cried. And Lin Xiaoran cried very easily.

“You brought milk tea?” she asked, eyes brightening.

Yichen handed her the warm cup from his coat pocket.

“Half sugar. No pearls.”

“Good boyfriend.” She pinched his cheek with satisfaction.

“You say that like you’re reviewing customer service.”

“I am.”

He laughed softly while she drank happily beside him, kicking her legs against the bench. From the rooftop door, their friends watched with disgust.

“Every day,” Chen Yuhao sighed.

Beside him, Tang Meilin rolled her eyes.

“You’re just jealous because you don’t have a girlfriend.”

Yuhao instantly straightened.

“That’s rude.”

Meanwhile, Xiaoran noticed them and waved.

“Why are you both standing there like divorced parents?”

“Because watching you two gives me diabetes,” Yuhao replied.

Yichen only smiled again. Meilin crossed her arms.

“Actually, Xiaoran, you should appreciate him more. If my future boyfriend tolerated even half your nonsense, I’d build him a temple.”

“I’m perfectly appreciative,” Xiaoran declared.

Yichen raised a brow.

“Really?”

“Yes.”

She was cute in a way that made people forgive her far too easily. Yichen most of all.

✦ ✦ ✦

The problem started a week later. Basketball practice had just ended when Xiaoran came to the gym carrying snacks for Yichen. The gym still smelled of floor polish and sweat, and the last few players were dragging the ball cart back to the storeroom. But the moment she entered, she saw a girl from Class 2 handing him a towel. Pretty. Tall. Elegant. Exactly Xiaoran’s least favorite type. The girl smiled softly.

“Your game today was amazing.”

“Thanks,” Yichen replied politely.

That should have been the end. But inside Lin Xiaoran’s head, jealousy was very loud. She walked over with a sweet smile that already made Yuhao—watching from nearby—mutter:

“Oh no.”

Xiaoran wrapped herself around Yichen’s arm possessively.

“Yichen,” she said brightly, “who’s this?”

The girl introduced herself politely. Xiaoran smiled even wider.

“Ohhh, you’re the girl who confessed to him last semester, right?”

Silence. The girl’s face stiffened. Yuhao covered his face with both hands. Even Yichen’s smile disappeared. Xiaoran continued casually:

“You’re still trying?”

“Xiaoran,” Yichen said quietly.

That tone alone made her pause. The girl looked close to tears as she hurried away. And suddenly the gym felt cold. Yichen gently removed Xiaoran’s arms from his sleeve.

“You went too far.”

Her chest tightened.

“What? I was joking.”

“It wasn’t funny.”

“She likes you.”

“And?” His voice stayed calm, which somehow felt worse. “That doesn’t mean you get to humiliate her.”

Xiaoran’s eyes went red. Yichen sighed internally the second he saw it. Because there it was. The tears. Always so fast.

“I’m not scolding you,” he said, more gently.

“But you’re angry.”

“I don’t like what you did.”

“You care more about her feelings than mine?”

“That’s not what I said.”

But Xiaoran already looked devastated.

“I was jealous,” she whispered.

Yichen rubbed his forehead.

“I know. But jealousy isn’t an excuse to hurt someone.”

She bit her lip hard, eyes watery. And then the worst possible thing happened.

“You’re being mean to me…”

Yichen nearly lost the argument right there. Lin Xiaoran crying was the one thing he had no defense against. He made himself stay firm anyway.

“Xiaoran. Don’t avoid the point.”

The tears spilled over. Great. Now he felt like the villain in a tragic romance drama. She turned and ran out of the gym before he could stop her. Yuhao walked over slowly.

“…You survived longer than expected.”

“Shut up.”

“You made her cry.”

“I KNOW.”

✦ ✦ ✦

Lin Xiaoran ignored him for two days. Which meant: no waiting outside his classroom. No stealing his drinks. No dramatic good morning voice messages. No random “Do you love me more today or yesterday?” questions. Half the school noticed how miserable Zhou Yichen looked.

“He looks like a ghost haunting his own desk,” Yuhao commented.

“Go apologize already,” Meilin said.

“I’m not apologizing for telling her she was wrong.”

“But you’re suffering.”

Yichen leaned back in frustration. The truth was, he missed her. He even missed being annoyed by her.

That evening, he finally found her sitting alone behind the library, hugging her knees, sleeves pulled down over her hands the way she always did when she was sulking. The moment she saw him, she looked away.

“I’m still angry.”

“I know. You said so in seventeen messages.”

Her lips twitched slightly before she hid it again. Yichen sat beside her quietly. For a moment, neither spoke. Then he sighed softly.

“Xiaoran.”

Silence.

“I’m sorry I was harsh.”

She sniffed. Here we go again.

“But,” he continued gently, “you really hurt her feelings.”

“I know…”

“And if someone treated you like that?”

“I’d cry for ten business days.”

Despite himself, Yichen laughed. Xiaoran finally looked at him, eyes still watery.

“I just hated seeing her near you.”

“I know.”

“She looked so pretty.”

“You’re prettier.”

“That answer was too fast.”

“Because it’s true.”

Her ears turned pink. Yichen reached over and pulled her closer by the sleeve.

“You can be jealous,” he murmured. “But don’t become cruel because of it.”

Xiaoran lowered her head guiltily.

“…Okay.”

“And no more embarrassing people publicly.”

“…Okay.”

“And no crying every time I correct you.”

“I can’t control that.”

“You absolutely can.”

“I’m delicate.”

“You’re evil.”

She gasped.

“You said you wouldn’t scold me anymore.”

Yichen sighed with complete defeat before pulling her into his arms anyway. She melted against him like a satisfied cat.

“You spoil her too much,” Meilin called from somewhere nearby.

The two looked up to find Yuhao and Meilin holding convenience store snacks while spying openly. Yuhao pointed accusingly.

“See? THIS is why she acts like a menace.”

Yichen didn’t even deny it. Xiaoran looked extremely pleased with herself. Then she tilted her head up at Yichen sweetly.

“You still love me?”

He looked down at her. She knew exactly what she was doing to him.

“Unfortunately,” he said, kissing her forehead lightly, “way too much.”
chapters.epigraph: “Some people are impossible to handle—and impossible not to love.”

chapters.desc: A claw machine, a chance meeting, and one boy who smiled like he already knew she was meant to stay.
chapters.title: Strawberry Milk Confession
chapters.content:
It started with a claw machine. Lin Xiaoran stood in the arcade with her arms crossed, glaring at the stupid plush bunny trapped behind the glass like it had insulted her whole family. Around her, the machines flashed and jingled, and somewhere behind her a group of middle schoolers were screaming over a racing game.

“This machine is rigged.”

“It’s not,” said a calm voice beside her.

She turned. And for half a second, she forgot what she’d been about to say. The boy standing there was tall, clean-looking, dressed in their school uniform with his sleeves rolled up. Sharp brows. Pretty eyes. The kind of face that got talked about in group chats. Most annoyingly, he was smiling. Not smug, not teasing. Just warm. Lin Xiaoran recovered quickly.

“You work for the machine company or something?”

The boy laughed softly.

“No. You’re just grabbing the bunny wrong.”

“I’ve tried eleven times.”

“That explains the problem.”

“What does THAT mean?”

“You’re impatient.”

She narrowed her eyes. Who even was this guy? The boy stepped beside her.

“Move.”

“Excuse me?”

“You want the bunny or not?”

Xiaoran shuffled aside and watched him suspiciously. He fed in a coin, adjusted the claw once—and won the bunny on the first try. Xiaoran gasped in betrayal.

“That’s impossible.”

He picked up the bunny and handed it to her.

“There.”

She hugged the plush automatically before catching herself.

“…Thank you.”

“You’re welcome.”

Then he smiled again. And for some reason, her heart skipped. It was very annoying.

“What’s your name?”

“Zhou Yichen.”

Oh. So this was THE Zhou Yichen. Top student. Basketball captain. Third-year legend. Girls from other schools literally waited outside games for him. Xiaoran’s guard went straight up.

“Hm. You’re overrated.”

Yichen blinked once. Then he laughed—properly, like she’d said something genuinely funny.

“You’re cute,” he said absentmindedly.

Lin Xiaoran nearly dropped the bunny.

“What?!”

“Nothing.”

His smile only deepened. And that was the first problem.

✦ ✦ ✦

After that, they somehow kept meeting everywhere. Library. Convenience store. Bus stop. School festival prep. It became suspicious enough that Tang Meilin accused fate of being too obvious.

“You like him,” Meilin declared.

“I absolutely do not.”

“You brushed your hair three times when he walked past.”

“That was wind maintenance.”

“That’s not a thing.”

Lin Xiaoran pretended not to hear. But secretly, she noticed things. Like how Zhou Yichen always looked relaxed around everyone else, but around her, he smiled more. How he remembered every tiny thing she said. How he once turned up with strawberry milk after hearing her complain that the cafeteria had been sold out for three days. How he never got annoyed even when she acted bratty on purpose. Which she did frequently.

“Move,” she’d say, shoving him aside in the hallway.

“You walked into me.”

“You exist in my path.”

“That sounds like a personal issue.”

“Hm.”

And somehow, he always looked amused instead of offended. It made her chest feel weird.

One rainy afternoon, Xiaoran forgot her umbrella after cram school.

By the time she reached the school gate, the rain was coming down in sheets, bouncing off the pavement.

“…Great.”

“You’ll get sick.”

She turned to find Zhou Yichen standing behind her holding a black umbrella. Again. Smiling, as usual.

“Were you waiting for someone?”

“You.”

Her heart stumbled so hard it was humiliating.

“…Why?”

“You texted the class group complaining about the rain.”

“That doesn’t mean come rescue me.”

“But you sounded pitiful.”

“I was NOT pitiful.”

“You used three crying emojis.”

“That’s expressive communication.”

Yichen laughed quietly before opening the umbrella over her head.

“Come on.”

The walk home became dangerous for Lin Xiaoran’s emotional stability. Zhou Yichen was gentle in ways she wasn’t prepared for. He tilted the umbrella toward her side. Walked closer to the road so passing cars wouldn’t splash her. Listened carefully even when she rambled nonsense. And worst of all, he looked at her like she mattered.

By the time they reached her apartment building, Xiaoran already knew she was doomed. Yichen looked down at her.

“You should go inside before you catch a cold.”

“…Okay.”

But neither moved. Rain poured softly around them. Xiaoran clutched the plush bunny still attached to her bag. Then suddenly blurted—

“Do you like me?”

Silence. Yichen blinked, clearly surprised. Unfortunately for her pride, nerves only made Lin Xiaoran more reckless.

“Because if you DON’T,” she rushed out, “then you should stop acting so nice to me all the time because it’s confusing.”

Yichen stared at her for two seconds. Then, slowly, he smiled. The smile that always made her weak.

“What if I do like you?”

Xiaoran’s brain stopped working.

“Oh.”

Very intelligent response. Yichen stepped closer under the umbrella. Up close, she could see his knuckles had gone white around the handle.

“What if I’ve liked you since the arcade?”

“…That fast?”

“You called me overrated within thirty seconds.”

“And that made you fall in love?”

“I found it refreshing.”

She stared at him, ears turning pink. This was bad. Now she wanted to say it too. And Lin Xiaoran hated being vulnerable. But she also hated lying. So after a full minute of silent suffering, she mumbled—

“…I like you too.”

Yichen’s whole face softened.

“Yeah?”

“I think about you too much,” she confessed with deep annoyance. “It’s affecting my studies.”

He laughed softly. And suddenly Xiaoran realized something that scared her a little. Zhou Yichen looked happiest when he was with her.

“Lin Xiaoran,” he said gently.

“…What?”

“Do you want to go out with me?”

Her eyes widened.

“So suddenly?”

“You confessed first.”

“That’s true.”

“And I don’t want anyone else asking you before I do.”

Her heart did something alarming. She tried to act calm anyway.

“Hm. I’ll consider it.”

Yichen raised a brow.

“You confessed two minutes ago.”

“That was before. This is negotiation.”

He laughed again, lowering his head slightly closer to hers.

“Okay then,” he murmured. “Please let me be your boyfriend.”

Xiaoran lasted exactly three seconds before smiling shyly.

“…Fine.”

“Fine?”

“Don’t push your luck, Zhou Yichen.”

“Yes, girlfriend.”

And hearing him say it for the first time felt warmer than the umbrella over their heads.
chapters.epigraph: “He found her in chaos, and stayed like it was home.”

chapters.desc: Zhou Yichen noticed her long before she noticed him—loud, chaotic, impossible to forget—and quietly decided she would become his favorite coincidence.
chapters.title: All Our Coincidences Were Intentional
chapters.content:
Before Zhou Yichen ever spoke to Lin Xiaoran, he already knew three things about her. First, she was loud. Second, she was dramatic. Third, she could cry faster than anyone he had ever met.

The first time he noticed her was outside the teachers’ office. A girl in a slightly messy uniform stood there arguing with a teacher over confiscated snacks.

“But instant noodles are emotionally necessary,” she protested.

“They are not.”

“What if I faint from heartbreak during math class?”

“You won’t.”

“How can you be so sure?”

At first, Yichen had only been walking past. Then the girl sighed and muttered under her breath—

“This school suppresses artistic souls.”

The teacher nearly laughed despite herself. Yichen did too. The girl was cute. Not just pretty—every single thing she felt showed on her face. That should’ve been the end of it. But after noticing someone once, somehow you kept seeing them everywhere. In the cafeteria complaining because her pudding was sold out. In the hallway fake-crying because her friend Tang Meilin refused to lend her lip gloss. In class presentations confidently speaking nonsense with full conviction.

“She’s ridiculous,” Chen Yuhao commented one afternoon while the basketball team walked past the courtyard.

Below them, Lin Xiaoran sat on a bench sulking while Meilin ignored her.

“What happened?” Yichen asked.

“She lost rock-paper-scissors.”

“…That’s why she looks heartbroken?”

“She takes competition seriously.”

Yichen watched as Xiaoran grabbed Meilin’s sleeve and whined something shameless enough to make Meilin shove her away. Instead of getting angry, Xiaoran just laughed, loud and careless, like she had never once worried what anyone thought of her. Yichen looked away after a second. For some reason, he was smiling.

✦ ✦ ✦

The second time she truly caught his attention was during rain duty week. Students rushed through the corridors while teachers yelled about slippery floors. Yichen carried sports equipment back toward the gym when he noticed a familiar figure crouching beside the school garden. Lin Xiaoran was crouched in the rain with a tiny soaked kitten tucked inside her jacket, her own hair dripping.

“What are you doing?” Meilin asked beside her.

“It looked cold.”

“You’re also cold.”

“I’m emotionally stronger than him.”

The kitten meowed pitifully. Xiaoran looked devastated.

“Oh no,” she whispered, hugging it carefully. “Don’t sound so pitiful.”

Yichen laughed quietly before he could stop himself. Xiaoran looked up. Their eyes met for the first time. Yichen saw her properly then. Soft features. Bright eyes. Pink lips slightly parted in surprise. For one second, Xiaoran simply stared. Then her eyes narrowed.

“…Why are you laughing?”

“Nothing.”

“You definitely laughed at me.”

“A little.”

“Hm. Rude.”

But she didn’t actually sound offended. Yichen walked away afterward. But he kept thinking about her. About how she held the kitten so gently. About how expressive her face was. About how alive she felt compared to everyone else around him.

✦ ✦ ✦

The arcade encounter one week later wasn’t exactly coincidence. Well. Not entirely. The basketball team had won a practice match nearby, and Yuhao suggested going to the shopping center arcade afterward. Yichen normally would’ve refused. But walking past the claw machines, he stopped. There she was again. Lin Xiaoran. Standing before a claw machine with absolute fury on her face.

“I’ve already spent twenty-seven yuan,” she told Meilin.

“Then stop.”

“No.”

“The bunny looks ugly anyway.”

“Don’t insult him.”

Yichen watched silently from several machines away. Xiaoran failed again. And again. Then she crouched in front of the machine and pointed accusingly.

“You and I are enemies now.”

Meilin looked exhausted.

“You’re talking to a machine.”

“It started first.”

Yichen laughed quietly. Before he knew it, he was walking toward her.

“You’re grabbing the bunny wrong.”

Xiaoran spun around. Yichen almost smiled. It was exactly the face she’d made defending instant noodles to the teacher.

“You work for the machine company or something?” she demanded.

And just like that, they were talking.

✦ ✦ ✦

After the arcade, the “coincidences” started piling up. Except most of them were caused by Zhou Yichen himself. He simply never admitted it. Like the convenience store encounter. Xiaoran entered after school craving strawberry milk only to discover the shelf empty.

“This country has failed me,” she sighed.

A hand appeared beside her, holding the exact drink.

“You can have mine.”

She turned. Zhou Yichen stood there as if this were fate, and not because he’d bought the last bottle ten minutes earlier, knowing the store was almost out.

“…Why are you here?”

“Buying water.”

“You bought strawberry milk.”

“I wanted this earlier. But not anymore.”

She laughed despite herself. Right then, Yichen decided he wanted to make her laugh as often as possible.

✦ ✦ ✦

Then came the library coincidence. Which was definitely not coincidence. Yuhao had mentioned that Xiaoran studied there every Wednesday, because her home WiFi died every week for “mysterious reasons.” The mysterious reason turned out to be her neighbor, who had been stealing it to download pirated games. So, naturally, Yichen started studying there every Wednesday too.

The first time Xiaoran spotted him, she squinted at him.

“You’re everywhere.”

“That sounds romantic.”

“That sounds creepy.”

He smiled lazily.

“Then I’ll leave.”

“…I didn’t say leave.”

Yichen sat back down. Xiaoran looked horrified at herself for saying that out loud. He nearly laughed.

✦ ✦ ✦

Then came the bus stop coincidence. The café coincidence. The hallway coincidence. The school festival coincidence.

At first, Xiaoran genuinely believed fate kept pushing them together.

Meanwhile, Yuhao watched Yichen deliberately take the long way between classes just to “accidentally” run into Xiaoran near Building C.

“You’re actually shameless,” Yuhao said.

“I don’t know what you mean.”

“You changed your entire lunch schedule because she eats earlier.”

“Coincidence.”

“You hate the cafeteria before noon.”

“People change.”

Yichen rubbed the back of his neck, which was what he always did when he was lying. Yuhao stared at him in disbelief. Zhou Yichen—calm, rational, untouchable Zhou Yichen—was staging run-ins like the lead in a romance drama. And he looked happy doing it. The moment she came into view, his whole expression changed. His smile went warm and easy, like she’d brought the sun in with her and didn’t know it.

One afternoon, Yuhao finally asked the obvious question.

“What exactly do you like about her so much?”

Yichen looked toward the courtyard below. Lin Xiaoran was down there again, complaining about something while Meilin ate her lunch in peace. Probably another crisis. Yichen watched her for a moment, smiling without realizing it.

“She makes everything feel less tiring.”

Yuhao blinked. Below them, Xiaoran happened to look up. Their eyes met across the courtyard. Her whole face lit up, like she was happy to see him and hadn’t noticed yet. Yichen smiled wider. And right then, he knew he was in serious trouble.
chapters.epigraph: “Before he ever spoke to her, he had already started choosing her.”

chapters.desc: Lin Xiaoran thought she understood Zhou Yichen completely… until she saw what his silence looked like when someone else tried to take his place.
chapters.title: The Day Zhou Yichen Finally Got Jealous
chapters.content:
The first sign something was wrong was that Zhou Yichen stopped smiling. Not completely. Just… less. And for someone like Zhou Yichen, who usually looked at Lin Xiaoran like she personally invented happiness, the difference was obvious to everyone. Everyone except Lin Xiaoran.

“Yichen,” she announced proudly during lunch, “someone confessed to me today.”

Chen Yuhao choked on his drink. Tang Meilin slowly lowered her spoon. Across the table, Zhou Yichen looked up calmly.

“Oh?”

Xiaoran nodded.

“A first-year boy.”

“…Mm.”

“He said I’m cute.”

“…He’s right.”

Yuhao glanced at Yichen’s hand. He was holding his chopsticks a little too tightly. That answer was far too calm. Xiaoran carried on happily, with no idea what she was walking into.

“Then he asked if I wanted to watch a movie with him.”

“What did you say?” Meilin asked carefully.

“I told him I already have a boyfriend, obviously.”

Yichen nodded once.

“Good.”

“But then,” Xiaoran added while opening her yogurt, “he got sad so I comforted him a little.”

Silence. Yuhao became very interested in his food. Yichen smiled faintly.

“What does ‘comforted him a little’ mean?”

“Oh, nothing serious.” Xiaoran waved casually. “I just told him he’ll definitely find someone prettier and kinder than me someday.”

Yichen stared at her.

“Prettier than you?”

“Yes.”

“You told another guy that?”

Xiaoran blinked.

“…Should I not?”

Meilin closed her eyes briefly. Oh no. The problem with Zhou Yichen was that he almost never got jealous. Girls liked him, confessed to him, and texted him all the time. Xiaoran got jealous about it at least twice a month. Yichen stayed calm through all of it—secure, and endlessly patient with her. So when he finally did get jealous, nobody knew what to expect.

✦ ✦ ✦

The second sign something was wrong came after school. Zhou Yichen waited outside Xiaoran’s classroom every afternoon. Today, he wasn’t there. Confused, Xiaoran wandered around Building B looking for him. She finally found him near the basketball court, talking with his teammates.

“Yichen!”

He looked over. Same handsome face. Same small smile. But something about him felt cooler. Further away. Xiaoran didn’t like it at all. She walked over and grabbed his sleeve out of habit.

“Why didn’t you wait for me?”

“I was busy.”

That had literally never stopped him before. Xiaoran narrowed her eyes.

“…Are you angry?”

“No.”

That was a lie, even if he told it nicely. Before she could investigate further, another voice interrupted.

“Senior Xiaoran!”

Everyone turned. A younger boy jogged over with a can of coffee, looking nervous. The same first-year. He faltered when he saw Zhou Yichen standing beside her. But he worked up his courage and held the drink out to Xiaoran.

“Thank you for earlier,” he said shyly.

“I bought your favorite flavor.”

Xiaoran looked surprised.

“How did you know my favorite?”

“You mentioned it.”

“Oh.”

She reached for it without thinking—only for another hand to take it first. Silence. Zhou Yichen held the can in one hand, smiling politely. It was not a friendly smile.

“Thank you,” he said gently. “But she doesn’t drink coffee after 5 p.m.”

The younger boy froze completely. Xiaoran blinked.

“…I do sometimes.”

Yichen looked at her.

“You couldn’t sleep until two last time.”

“…Oh.”

The boy was starting to sweat.

“I-I just wanted to thank senior…”

“You already did.” Yichen’s voice stayed pleasant. “That’s enough.”

Even Yuhao, watching from nearby, nearly saluted. That was the most boyfriend move he had ever seen. The boy made his escape. As soon as he was gone, Xiaoran turned to Yichen.

“…You scared him.”

“He’ll survive.”

“…You’re definitely angry.”

“I said I’m not.”

“You’re doing your fake customer-service smile.”

Yuhao walked off. He did not want to witness whatever happened next.

✦ ✦ ✦

That night, Lin Xiaoran lay sprawled across her bed, video calling Meilin.

“I think Zhou Yichen is malfunctioning.”

“He’s jealous.”

“…Huh?”

Meilin stared at her through the screen.

“You really don’t notice things unless they hit you with a chair.”

“What’s there to notice?”

“He’s obsessed with you.”

“Well, yes. Obviously.”

“And another guy openly approached you.”

“But I rejected him!”

“You also comforted him.”

“He looked sad!”

Meilin sighed.

“Xiaoran. Imagine a pretty girl confessed to Yichen, then Yichen comforted her gently and accepted gifts from her.”

Xiaoran sat bolt upright.

“…Oh.”

“Exactly.”

Suddenly, everything replayed in her head. Yichen not waiting after class. The weird smile. Taking the coffee. The calm voice that somehow felt colder than usual. Oh no. Zhou Yichen was jealous. And for some reason, knowing that made her chest feel warm. Which was probably not the right reaction.

✦ ✦ ✦

The next morning, Xiaoran arrived at school carrying two strawberry milks. One for herself. One peace offering. She found Zhou Yichen in the library before morning class, reading quietly near the windows. Sunlight fell across his face. He looked annoyingly good. Xiaoran crept over and set the drink down beside him.

“For you.”

Yichen glanced at it.

“Bribery?”

“Yes.”

He laughed quietly despite himself. Good. Progress. Xiaoran sat beside him, fidgeting slightly.

“…Are you still jealous?”

“I wasn’t jealous.”

He rubbed the back of his neck.

“Liar.”

“I was concerned.”

“You stole his coffee like a drama villain.”

“He bought it for my girlfriend.”

The way he said my girlfriend so naturally made her ears go warm. Yichen finally closed his book and looked at her properly.

“I trust you,” he said. “I just don’t like other guys trying to take my place.”

Xiaoran blinked slowly.

“…That’s kind of hot.”

For the first time, Yichen looked genuinely caught off guard. Then he laughed helplessly, covering his eyes briefly.

“You’re unbelievable.”

“No but seriously,” Xiaoran continued, leaning closer. “You’re usually so calm. Seeing you jealous is kind of…”

“Kind of?”

“…Cute.”

Yichen stared at her.

“I was miserable yesterday.”

“You looked good being miserable.”

“That doesn’t help.”

Xiaoran giggled before hooking her pinky around his sleeve.

“Don’t worry,” she said softly. “I only like you.”

His expression softened. There it was—the look he only ever gave her, no matter how jealous, annoyed, or tired he was. Yichen sighed and pulled her chair closer to his.

“Next time,” he murmured, “don’t comfort random boys who like you.”

“What if I enjoy making you jealous?”

“You won’t enjoy the consequences.”

Xiaoran gasped.

“You’re threatening me?”

“I’m warning you.”

“That’s the same thing!”

Yichen leaned in, his voice low.

“Lin Xiaoran.”

“…What?”

“If another guy buys you coffee again, I’m kissing you in front of him.”

Silence. Her whole face went red. And Zhou Yichen finally smiled properly again, looking very satisfied with himself. That was when Lin Xiaoran realized, too late, that a jealous Zhou Yichen might be far more dangerous than she had ever been.
chapters.epigraph: “He was never jealous often—so when he was, even love felt dangerous.”

chapters.desc: She said it over a plate of shrimp, in front of witnesses, without meaning to—and Zhou Yichen was never going to let her take it back.
chapters.title: The First Time She Said “I Love You” Casually
chapters.epigraph: “The biggest words are sometimes the ones that slip out by accident.”
chapters.content:
Lin Xiaoran’s first “I love you” was not romantic. There was no rain, no heartfelt confession, no background music. It happened at a crowded hotpot place near school, because Zhou Yichen was peeling shrimp for her.

“You’re actually amazing,” Xiaoran declared from across the restaurant table.

Yichen kept peeling.

“You say that every time someone feeds you.”

“That’s because acts of service are attractive.”

“You learned one psychology term and became unbearable.”

“I love you.”

Silence. Xiaoran kept drinking her juice peacefully. Across from her, Zhou Yichen froze. The shrimp stopped halfway to her plate. Chen Yuhao slowly looked up from his noodles. Tang Meilin closed her eyes. Oh no. Lin Xiaoran clearly had no idea what she had just said. Zhou Yichen was staring at her.

“…What did you say?”

Xiaoran blinked. “Hm?”

Yuhao kicked her chair under the table.

“Ow?! What’s wrong with you?!”

“You just said you love him.”

“…And?”

Everyone stared at her in disbelief. Then Xiaoran finally processed her own sentence. Her eyes widened slowly.

“Oh.”

Yichen still hadn’t moved. He was just looking at her, very calmly. Xiaoran grabbed her juice cup with both hands.

“That slipped out accidentally.”

“You accidentally love me?”

“No—that’s not what I meant.”

“Then explain.”

Her face went red.

Meilin whispered to Yuhao, “This is the happiest day of his life.”

Yuhao nodded. “He’s pretending to stay calm, but inside he’s already planning the wedding.”

Meanwhile, Xiaoran was dying. Saying “I love you” by accident was somehow more embarrassing than any proper confession. Especially with Zhou Yichen looking at her like that—soft and focused, like nothing else in the restaurant existed.

“I got caught up in the moment,” she mumbled.

“You said you love me because I peeled shrimp.”

“That sounds shallow when you say it out loud.”

Yichen finally smiled—small at first, then wider. It was the smile Xiaoran secretly liked most.

“You’ve never said it before,” he said quietly.

The teasing at the table died down a little. Xiaoran looked away.

“…You already knew.”

“I did.”

“Then why are you acting surprised?”

“Knowing isn’t the same as hearing it.”

Her chest tightened, because he was right. They’d been dating for months. She asked him “Do you love me?” almost every day, usually right after doing something annoying, and he always answered. But she had never once said it herself. And now everyone at the table was staring at her, waiting.

“This is horrible,” she whispered.

Yuhao looked delighted. “Say it again.”

“I’ll kill you.”

Meilin sipped her drink calmly. “Personally, I think it’s cute.”

“Traitor.”

Yichen rested his chin against one hand, eyes still fixed on her.

“…Did you mean it?”

Lin Xiaoran wanted to evaporate. It wasn’t fair of him to ask so softly.

“…Maybe.”

“That’s not an answer.”

She tried to glare. “Why are you interrogating me?”

“Because I’m happy.”

That was the problem with him. No teasing, no smugness. He was just happy, plainly and honestly, because she loved him. Xiaoran’s ears turned even redder.

“…Fine,” she muttered. “I meant it.”

Yichen’s whole face softened. And Xiaoran realized, a little alarmed, that hearing “I love you” from her might be Zhou Yichen’s biggest weakness. He looked absurdly happy.

“You’re smiling too much,” she accused.

“You caused it.”

“That sounds like a you problem.”

Yuhao made a gagging noise.

“Can you two stop being disgusting while I’m eating?”

“No,” Yichen said.

The table went quiet. Zhou Yichen was polite to everyone, always. Right now, he was thriving.

Meilin looked impressed. “One accidental ‘I love you’ and he became arrogant.”

“I’m not arrogant,” Yichen said, still looking at Xiaoran like she was the only person at the table.

Xiaoran hid behind her menu.

“I regret speaking.”

“You can’t take it back.”

“I can try.”

“You said it in front of witnesses.”

“And I,” Yuhao added proudly, “will remember this forever.”

“I hate all of you.”

✦ ✦ ✦

The teasing went on for three days. Every time Xiaoran complained about homework—

“Maybe Yichen can help,” Yuhao would say. “Since you love him so much.”

Every time she bought snacks—

“Such loving girlfriend behavior,” Meilin would say.

Xiaoran nearly lost her mind. Zhou Yichen, meanwhile, was insufferable. He got even more affectionate than usual. Touching her head more. Holding her hand first. Smiling at her like she’d hung the moon. Worst of all, he kept bringing it up when they were alone.

“You love me,” he’d murmur out of nowhere.

And Xiaoran would go red all over again.

One evening after cram school, they walked home under an orange sky. Xiaoran kicked at pebbles while Yichen carried her bag, because apparently she was “too tired.”

“You’ve been smiling all week,” she accused.

“I wonder why.”

“I said it once accidentally.”

“You meant it.”

“…Unfortunately.”

Yichen laughed softly. After a moment, he spoke again, quietly.

“I love you too.”

Xiaoran stopped walking. She had blurted hers out over shrimp. He said his carefully, on purpose, like he wanted her to hear every word. The evening breeze moved gently around them. Xiaoran’s chest felt strangely full.

“You can’t say things like that so suddenly,” she mumbled.

“Why not?”

“It affects my emotional stability.”

“That sounds serious.”

“It IS serious.”

Yichen smiled and reached over to fix the crooked ribbon in her hair.

“But you already knew,” he teased softly.

Xiaoran stared at him for a moment. Then she buried her face in his shoulder.

“This relationship is ruining my cool image.”

“You never had one.”

“Mean.”

But she stayed where she was. Yichen held her close, smiling into her hair. He had a feeling he would remember that careless little “I love you” for the rest of his life.

chapters.desc: Zhou Yichen almost never gets angry. Then a teammate says the wrong thing about Lin Xiaoran, and he can’t let it go.
chapters.title: The One Time Zhou Yichen Lost His Temper
chapters.epigraph: “Gentle people have a line too. You just don’t see it until someone crosses it.”
chapters.content:
During basketball season, everyone knew to leave Zhou Yichen alone before a match. He got frighteningly competitive, and nobody was stupid enough to provoke him. Liu Zheng had never been good at reading a room.

“Pass the ball faster!”

Sneakers squeaked across the gym floor as the team ran drills before the regional tournament. Sweat dripped down Zhou Yichen’s neck as he snatched the ball back sharply.

“You were late to position,” he said coldly.

Liu Zheng scoffed. “You act like we’re professionals.”

“Then stop playing carelessly.”

The air in the gym tightened. Nearby, Chen Yuhao sighed. Basketball Zhou Yichen and boyfriend Zhou Yichen were basically two separate people. Off the court, he was patient and gentle and always smiling. On the court, he was focused enough to make grown adults nervous. Today, his patience was especially thin.

Coach Wang blew the whistle sharply. “Again!”

Practice resumed. Every failed pass made things worse between Yichen and Liu Zheng. At the water break, it finally boiled over. Liu Zheng tossed his towel aside irritably.

“Why are you acting so insane lately?” he muttered. “You only care because your girlfriend keeps watching your games.”

Yuhao’s head snapped up. Yichen didn’t respond. Which somehow felt worse. Liu Zheng laughed, oblivious.

“I mean seriously, if I had a girlfriend looking like Lin Xiaoran, I’d show off too.”

Silence. A loose ball rolled away across the floor. Nobody went after it.

Yuhao stood up. “Okay, maybe stop talking now—”

But Liu Zheng kept going.

“Honestly though, Xiaoran’s body is kinda—”

Yichen hurled the ball at the wall so hard the bang echoed through the whole gym. Everyone froze. Zhou Yichen stood there breathing hard, jaw tight enough to hurt. Nobody on the team had ever seen him like this. Not annoyed, not irritated. Furious.

“Say another word,” Yichen said quietly, “and I’ll break your teeth.”

Nobody moved. Zhou Yichen did not talk like that. Ever. Even Coach Wang looked shocked.

Liu Zheng went pale. “I was joking.”

“You don’t joke about her like that.”

His voice stayed low and controlled, which was somehow scarier. Yuhao stepped between them before anyone could do something stupid.

“Okay, enough. Zheng, shut up. Right now.”

Liu Zheng muttered an apology and backed off. But the damage was already done. Zhou Yichen couldn’t calm down.

✦ ✦ ✦

Their first tournament match that afternoon was a disaster. Normally, Zhou Yichen dominated games effortlessly. That day, he played recklessly—too aggressive, too emotional. Every missed shot made him visibly angrier. Every mistake from teammates irritated him further.

By halftime, the whole team was falling apart. Coach Wang caught his arm by the bench.

“What’s wrong with you today?”

“I’m fine.”

“You’re playing like you want to fight someone.”

Yichen said nothing. Across the court, Liu Zheng wouldn’t look at him. The team lost by eleven points.

The next day’s match was even worse. Yichen argued with teammates, ignored the plays, and nearly started another fight when someone shoved him going for a rebound. They lost again. Yuhao had never seen him like this. It wasn’t the losing, or the pressure. It was because someone had talked about Lin Xiaoran like that. And he couldn’t let it go.

✦ ✦ ✦

By the third day, even Coach Wang looked exhausted.

“This can’t continue,” he told Yuhao quietly during practice break.

Yuhao sighed. “I know.”

“Talk to him.”

“I tried.”

“And?”

“He stared at me until I left.”

Coach Wang rubbed his forehead. Zhou Yichen was usually the easiest player he had—disciplined, calm, reliable. But anything involving Lin Xiaoran apparently switched off his common sense.

Practice ended early after another terrible scrimmage. Most of the team cleared out fast. Only Yuhao stayed. Yichen sat alone by the bleachers, elbows on his knees, still wound tight. A ball sat untouched by his feet. He hadn’t taken a single shot since practice ended. Yuhao sat down next to him.

“You know Xiaoran would hate seeing you like this.”

Silence.

“She’d probably cry actually.”

Nothing. Then finally—

“I know.”

Yuhao sighed.

“Then why are you acting insane?”

Yichen stared at the floor.

“…Because I can’t stand hearing people talk about her like that.”

Yuhao’s expression softened slightly. And honestly, he understood. Everyone knew how much Zhou Yichen adored Lin Xiaoran. Not in a possessive way. He was just protective of her, like she was something he wanted to keep away from anything ugly.

“She’s not some topic for locker room jokes,” Yichen muttered.

“I know.”

“And I know he didn’t mean serious harm.” His jaw tightened again. “But hearing him say her name like that…”

He didn’t finish. Just remembering it made him angry all over again. Yuhao sighed.

“You’re still letting it ruin everything.”

“…I know.”

Knowing didn’t fix anything.

✦ ✦ ✦

The solution arrived the next afternoon wearing a pink hoodie and carrying strawberry milk. Lin Xiaoran slipped quietly into the empty gym. When Zhou Yichen saw her, his expression eased a little. Softer, less sharp. Still upset, though. Xiaoran walked toward him slowly.

“…Hi.”

“Why are you here?”

“Checking if my boyfriend murdered someone.”

Yichen almost smiled. Good enough. Xiaoran sat down beside him, hugging her knees. Meilin had already told her everything: Liu Zheng, the comment, the near-fights, and Yichen wrecking the team’s morale over it. Part of her was secretly touched. The other part wanted to bonk him with a textbook.

“You lost two matches,” she said softly.

“…Mm.”

“Coach Wang looks like he aged ten years.”

Silence. Then Xiaoran poked his cheek.

“You’re stupid.”

Yichen finally looked at her properly.

“…Excuse me?”

“You heard me.”

“That’s harsh.”

“So is the way you’ve been acting.”

He looked away again. Xiaoran’s voice went gentler.

“Yichen.”

“…What?”

“I know why you’re angry.”

His fingers tightened slightly against his knee.

“But you don’t need to destroy yourself over it.”

The gym was quiet. Then after a moment—

“I hated hearing him talk about you like that.”

Xiaoran’s face softened. He didn’t sound proud or angry anymore. He just sounded hurt, like someone had dirtied something he loved. She moved closer until their shoulders touched lightly.

“You know what the funny thing is?”

“What?”

“I wasn’t even there.”

Yichen frowned slightly.

“So?”

“So if I’m not hurt,” she said gently, “why are you suffering this much alone?”

That hit harder than anything Coach Wang had said. Yichen lowered his eyes. Xiaoran reached over and hooked her pinky around his hand.

“You getting angry for me is nice,” she said. “But ruining yourself for it isn’t.”

“…I couldn’t calm down.”

“I know.”

“And every time I remembered it—”

“I know.”

She rubbed her thumb lightly over his fingers.

“I’m okay,” she whispered.

Slowly, the tightness in his chest began to ease. Yichen let out a long breath and leaned back against the bleachers.

“You’re really not upset?”

“I mean,” Xiaoran said thoughtfully, “if someone described my boyfriend like that, I’d also become violent.”

Yichen laughed. It was small, but it was real. Xiaoran brightened.

“There he is.”

Yichen looked at her helplessly.

“You fixed my mood too easily.”

“That’s because you love me.”

“…Unfortunately.”

She gasped. “Wow.”

But she shifted closer anyway, and his arm slid around her waist. After a moment, Xiaoran spoke quietly against his shoulder.

“Next game,” she murmured, “win instead.”

Yichen looked down at her.

“For me?”

“No.” She smiled slightly. “For yourself.”

Yichen kissed her forehead.

“…Okay.”

It was only one word, but he meant it.

chapters.desc: Zhou Yichen is leaving on a family trip for seven days. Lin Xiaoran is handling it terribly.
chapters.title: The Week Lin Xiaoran Became Unbearably Clingy
chapters.epigraph: “Seven days isn’t long—unless you’re counting.”
chapters.content:
A week before the Zhou family vacation, Zhou Yichen noticed something strange. Lin Xiaoran had turned up at basketball practice four times in two days.

“Xiaoran,” Yichen said while tying his shoelaces, “why are you sitting here again?”

She sat cross-legged on the gym floor eating chips peacefully.

“I’m supporting youth athletics.”

“You booed the opposing team during practice.”

“They looked arrogant.”

“They’re our second-string players.”

“Still.”

Yichen gave her a long look. Because lately, Lin Xiaoran had become absurdly clingy. Not her normal level of clingy. Advanced clingy. Hugging his arm every five minutes, stealing his jackets, following him between classes. Even Chen Yuhao had noticed.

“She’s attached to you like a haunted doll.”

“I heard that,” Xiaoran said, leaning against Yichen’s shoulder.

“That proves my point.”

Yichen looked down at her.

“…Did something happen?”

“No.”

“Then why have you been acting weird all week?”

“I’m not weird.”

“You cried yesterday because I went to buy water without telling you.”

“I thought you disappeared emotionally.”

Yuhao gagged loudly. But Yichen was starting to understand. Next week, he would be gone. His family was going overseas for seven days before final semester preparations began. Seven days wasn’t long. It was apparently long enough for Lin Xiaoran to go into full crisis mode.

✦ ✦ ✦

It got worse every day.

On Monday, Xiaoran turned up outside Yichen’s classroom at break with snacks.

“For you.”

“You only buy snacks when you want something.”

“I’m investing emotionally.”

On Tuesday, she stole his hoodie during lunch and refused to return it.

“It smells like you,” she explained shamelessly.

“That sounds mildly concerning.”

On Wednesday, she draped herself across his desk during study period.

“Yichen.”

“Hm?”

“What if you forget me during vacation?”

He looked up slowly.

“…Lin Xiaoran.”

“What?”

“That might be the dumbest thing you’ve ever said.”

She frowned. “Wow.”

“I’m serious.”

“You’ll meet pretty foreign girls.”

“I’m not going abroad to start a harem.”

“You don’t know the future.”

Yichen sighed and reached over to pinch her cheek.

“Why are you overthinking so much?”

Xiaoran looked away and mumbled something. The truth was embarrassing. She simply hated the idea of not seeing him for a week. Which was ridiculous. Pathetic, even. But Zhou Yichen had quietly become part of her daily routine. Morning messages. Walking home together. Sharing drinks, stealing his sleeves, listening to him laugh at her nonsense. What was she supposed to do for seven whole days without annoying him? Tragic.

✦ ✦ ✦

By Thursday, even Tang Meilin had had enough.

“You’ve called him fourteen times today.”

“I miss him.”

“He went home thirty minutes ago.”

“Exactly.”

Meilin closed her planner and stared at her.

“You need psychological help.”

Yichen, for his part, found it exhausting. And secretly adorable. Because every time Xiaoran acted clingy, she looked completely unaware of how obvious her feelings were.

Like now: Friday afternoon, the day before his flight. Yichen sat in the library trying to finish practice exams while Xiaoran quietly occupied the chair beside him. She hadn’t said a word in ten minutes, which was alarming. Yichen finally looked over. She was hugging his arm and staring sadly at his sleeve.

“…Are you mourning?”

“Maybe.”

He laughed—the helpless laugh he only ever did around her. Xiaoran’s grip tightened.

“See?” she accused quietly.

“See what?”

“You laugh too easily when I’m around.”

“And?”

“What if next week you laugh like that with someone else?”

Yichen closed his book. Okay. This had gone far enough.

“Come here,” he said softly.

Xiaoran blinked, then scooted closer. Yichen looked at her carefully.

“You really think I’ll suddenly stop loving you after seven days?”

“…Maybe not stop.”

“Then?”

“You’ll be less used to me.”

For a second, Yichen honestly didn’t know whether to laugh or kiss her. Possibly both. Instead, he gently squeezed her hand.

“Lin Xiaoran.”

“Hm?”

“You know what I think?”

“What?”

“I think you’re too used to me spoiling you.”

She gasped.

“That sounds like YOUR fault.”

“Probably.”

Xiaoran leaned against him. After a moment—

“…Can I call you every day?”

“You already do that.”

“More.”

“How much more?”

“Like, a lot more.”

Yichen laughed again.

✦ ✦ ✦

The day at the airport was worse. The departure hall was all rolling suitcases and boarding announcements, and Xiaoran looked one step away from tears the entire morning. Yuhao found it hilarious.

“You look like he’s being deployed to war.”

“He’s abandoning me internationally.”

“It’s seven days.”

“That’s basically a month.”

Yichen stood beside his luggage, watching her spiral with growing amusement. His mother noticed too.

“She’s cute,” Mrs. Zhou whispered to him.

Yichen smiled helplessly. “Very.”

Near the departure gate, Xiaoran clung to his sleeve, pouting.

“You better miss me.”

“I already do.”

“You haven’t even left yet.”

“Exactly.”

Her ears went pink. Then Xiaoran’s face fell again.

“…What if something fun happens and I’m not there?”

Yichen reached over and fixed her messy hair gently.

“Nothing is more fun than you.”

Silence. Yuhao pretended to throw up. Mrs. Zhou looked delighted. Xiaoran went completely still, then hid her face in his shoulder.

“You can’t say things like that right before you leave.”

“Why not?”

“Because now I’m going to cry at the gate.”

Yichen smiled and hugged her—warm and safe and familiar, exactly what Xiaoran was going to miss all week.

“I’ll come back soon,” he murmured into her hair.

“…Promise?”

“Promise.”

Then, after a pause—

“And Xiaoran?”

“What?”

“You’re allowed to miss me normally.”

She looked up suspiciously.

“What does that mean?”

“It means stop acting like I’m dying.”

“…No promises.”

Yichen laughed and kissed her forehead. Somehow, that tiny kiss almost made Lin Xiaoran cry harder than the goodbye itself.

chapters.desc: One week apart, one airport reunion, and Lin Xiaoran is not prepared for how good her boyfriend looks.
chapters.title: The Day Zhou Yichen Came Back Looking Illegal
chapters.epigraph: “Absence makes the heart grow fonder—and apparently the boyfriend more handsome.”
chapters.content:
Lin Xiaoran made a decision the moment she woke up that morning. She would NOT cry at the airport reunion. She had dignity. Class. Emotional maturity. Tang Meilin laughed for a full thirty seconds after hearing this.

“You cried because he changed his profile picture last week.”

“That was emotional shock.”

“He literally just wore glasses.”

“Exactly.”

Then Zhou Yichen came back, and things got much worse. Somehow, after only one week away, he had come back even more handsome. Offensively handsome. She realized it the moment she spotted him at the arrival gate. Black hoodie. Hands in pockets. Slightly messy hair from the flight. Tall enough to stand out immediately in the crowd. Then he looked up, saw her, and smiled. Oh. Oh no. Lin Xiaoran’s soul nearly left her body.

“Why does he look like that,” she whispered.

Meilin looked up from her phone. “Like what?”

“Like a male lead with financial stability.”

“What does that even mean?”

“I don’t know but I’m suffering.”

Zhou Yichen had already spotted her, frozen beside the gate. His smile widened. And somehow THAT made it worse. She had missed him all week—his voice, his laugh, his stupid calm face. But her memory had left out one important detail. Zhou Yichen was even better looking in motion. Walking toward her now with his luggage, sleeves pushed up his forearms, he looked illegal.

“Why are you standing there like a statue?” Meilin asked.

“I forgot how to breathe.”

“You’re embarrassing.”

“I KNOW.”

Yichen had already reached them.

“Xiaoran.”

His voice was a little rough from the flight, and more familiar than home. Xiaoran stared up at him. Then she noticed more things. His hair was a little longer. His shoulders looked broader. He was slightly tanned. And his eyes went soft the second he saw her. This was horrible. Why was her own boyfriend attacking her with his face?

“…Hi,” she managed.

Yichen paused and blinked.

“…Why are you looking at me like that?”

Xiaoran pointed accusingly.

“You got more handsome.”

Silence. Meilin covered her face. Zhou Yichen laughed.

“There it is.”

“There WHAT is?”

“You missed me too much.”

“That’s not related.”

“It definitely is.”

He stepped closer and reached up to fix her messy bangs. Xiaoran nearly died on the spot. No. This was not okay.

“How are you prettier after a seven-day absence?” she demanded.

“Prettier?”

“Yes.”

“I’m a man.”

“And?”

Yichen smiled helplessly. Meilin walked away so she wouldn’t have to watch any more of this. Xiaoran kept staring at him in growing distress. He looked TOO good. Like one of those slow-motion drama edits people post online with sad music. Even random people at the airport kept glancing his way. Xiaoran’s territorial instincts kicked in. One nearby girl looked at him for two seconds too long. Xiaoran grabbed his sleeve. Yichen looked amused.

“…Hello to you too.”

“Don’t stand there attracting women.”

“I’m standing normally.”

“Too normally.”

Yichen laughed again. God. Even his laugh sounded handsome today. Xiaoran wanted to fight someone. Possibly herself.

✦ ✦ ✦

The ride home in the Zhou family car was exhausting. Mostly because Xiaoran could not stop staring at him.

At first, Yichen pretended not to notice. After twenty straight minutes—

“…Why do you keep looking at me?”

“I’m investigating.”

“That sounds concerning.”

“You changed.”

“How?”

“You upgraded.”

Yichen actually looked thoughtful for a second.

“…Was vacation that effective?”

“No. Your face is just doing too much.”

He laughed under his breath and leaned back against the seat.

“You’re dramatic.”

“You became hotter while abroad.”

“That sentence sounds insane.”

“I’m suffering sincerely.”

Yichen reached over and squeezed her hand. That small touch made Xiaoran’s chest ache a little. She had really missed him. More than she expected. Yichen noticed she had gone quiet.

“What’s wrong?”

“…Nothing.”

“Liar.”

Xiaoran looked out the window.

“I just missed you.”

The car went quiet. In the front seat, Mrs. Zhou turned the radio up a little and politely pretended not to listen. Yichen’s thumb brushed across her knuckles.

“I missed you too.”

Simple and honest. Hearing it in person was completely different from hearing it over the phone all week. Xiaoran leaned against his shoulder, clingy again, like she had gone seven years without affection instead of seven days. Yichen smiled and rested his head against hers. Comfortable silence filled the car.

“You smell different,” Xiaoran accused.

“…What?”

“You smell expensive now.”

Yichen looked genuinely confused.

“It’s probably hotel shampoo.”

“Hm.”

She narrowed her eyes and hugged his arm tighter.

“You’re not allowed to become any more handsome.”

“That’s a strange rule.”

“I’m serious.”

“Why?”

“Because I can’t take much more of this.”

Yichen laughed so hard he had to look away. And Xiaoran’s heart betrayed her all over again. How could one person look THAT good laughing? It was deeply unfair.

✦ ✦ ✦

That evening, Zhou Yichen found a string of messages from Chen Yuhao.

Yuhao: Did Xiaoran survive the reunion?

Yuhao: Meilin said she looked like she saw a celebrity boyfriend.

Yuhao: Actually worse. A celebrity boyfriend who peels shrimp.

Yichen smiled as he typed back.

Yichen: She stared at me for twenty minutes.

Yuhao: HAHAHAHA

Yuhao: She missed you too hard.

Yichen glanced up from his phone. Across his bedroom, Lin Xiaoran sat on the floor unpacking the snacks he had brought back for her. She was still wearing the hoodie she’d stolen before he left, and still giving him strange looks every few minutes. Then she looked up again.

“…You’re still handsome.”

Yichen laughed helplessly.

“Xiaoran.”

“What?”

“I’ve had the same face since last week.”

She pointed at him.

“No. This one feels internationally upgraded.”

chapters.desc: She only wanted to buy him pastries. She did not plan to get lost without her phone.
chapters.title: The Day Lin Xiaoran Got Horribly Lost
chapters.epigraph: “Some people find their way home with a map. She found hers by being found.”
chapters.content:
There were two things Lin Xiaoran should never be trusted with alone. First, important responsibilities. Second, directions. That Saturday afternoon, Zhou Yichen forgot both.

“Wait for me after the match,” he said, fixing his jersey by the gym entrance.

Xiaoran nodded, sipping her strawberry milk.

“I’m not a child.”

Chen Yuhao snorted. Yichen looked unconvinced. Lin Xiaoran’s sense of direction wasn’t just bad. It was catastrophic. She once got lost inside a shopping mall with only three floors. Another time she accidentally walked into the boys’ restroom because she “followed vibes.” So, naturally, Yichen worried.

“I’m serious,” he said carefully. “Don’t wander too far.”

Xiaoran gasped.

“You underestimate me.”

“Yes.”

“Wow.”

“I love you,” Yichen corrected calmly, “but you navigate like a confused pigeon.”

Yuhao nearly collapsed laughing. Xiaoran glared at him.

“I’ll have you know I survived seventeen years independently.”

“That’s honestly impressive.”

“YOU’RE BOTH MEAN.”

Yichen just smiled and leaned down a little.

“Just stay near the school area.”

“Hm.”

“And keep your phone with you.”

“Hm.”

“Actually listen when I speak.”

“Hm.”

“…You’re not listening.”

“I’m emotionally listening.”

Yichen sighed. He trusted her anyway. Big mistake.

✦ ✦ ✦

At first, everything went fine. The match started at two, and Xiaoran sat in the bleachers cheering loudly every time Yichen scored. Which was often. Basketball Zhou Yichen was a serious problem. Sweaty, focused, competitive—a real danger to her concentration.

After halftime, though, Xiaoran got restless. The gym was noisy and crowded, and she remembered a cute bakery she’d seen somewhere near school. A bakery sounded peaceful. And if she came back with snacks for Yichen, she would look like an excellent girlfriend. Perfect plan. Lin Xiaoran making plans on her own usually ended in disaster.

✦ ✦ ✦

Twenty minutes later, she realized something horrible.

“…This street wasn’t here before.”

Xiaoran stood at an unfamiliar intersection, holding two bags of pastries that still smelled of butter, and a growing sense of concern. Okay. Maybe she took one wrong turn. That was normal. Probably. She turned around confidently. Then she froze. All four roads looked equally unfamiliar.

“…Hm.”

Not ideal. Still manageable. Hopefully. Xiaoran kept walking, trying to remember landmarks. There was… A tree? Definitely some buildings. Maybe a cat earlier. This was useless. Ten more minutes passed. And then, on top of being lost, she realized something horrifying.

“My phone.”

Silence. Xiaoran checked her pockets frantically. Nothing. Her face went blank. No phone. No map. No way to call anyone. Her phone was still in her school bag, back at the gym.

“…Oh no.”

For the first time all day, she started to panic.

✦ ✦ ✦

Back at school, Zhou Yichen had already noticed something was wrong. The match had ended thirty minutes ago, and Lin Xiaoran was nowhere to be seen.

At first, Yichen stayed calm.

“She probably wandered off to the vending machines,” Yuhao said.

Yichen nodded once.

Five minutes later, she still wasn’t back.

Ten minutes later, Yichen had stopped smiling completely. Yichen called her. Somewhere behind the bleachers, a phone started ringing inside her school bag. Yuhao stared at the ringing bag. Lin Xiaoran without her phone was a genuine emergency. Yichen grabbed his bag.

“She was talking about some bakery last week,” he muttered.

Yuhao stood too. “I’ll check the east street.”

Coach Wang blinked as his star player walked out in the middle of the post-game talk.

“Where are you going?”

“Emergency.”

“What emergency?”

“…My girlfriend.”

Coach Wang, who had survived regionals, waved him off without another word.

✦ ✦ ✦

Lin Xiaoran, meanwhile, was losing her mind. Every person she asked for directions somehow made things worse.

“The school?” one uncle repeated. “Go straight then left.”

Which left? HOW left?

Another woman said, “Near the blue building.”

EVERY BUILDING WAS BLUE. At one point, she somehow ended up outside a laundromat. Why was there a laundromat?! She sat down on a bench, clutching her pastry bags and trying not to cry.

“This is how I die,” she whispered.

An old woman nearby gave her a worried look.

“Lin Xiaoran.”

Her head snapped up. Zhou Yichen was standing across the street, breathing hard, still in his basketball jersey, his hair a mess from running around. For one beautiful moment, Lin Xiaoran honestly thought he looked like a movie hero.

“YICHEN.”

She nearly ran into traffic. Yichen crossed quickly and caught her arm.

“Careful.”

The second she grabbed onto him, Xiaoran fell apart.

“I got lost,” she confessed miserably.

“I know.”

“I tried asking directions but everyone speaks in puzzles.”

Yichen looked like he wanted to laugh and sigh at the same time. Instead, he pulled her close.

“You scared me.”

That made her feel guilty right away. He really did look worried. Not annoyed. Worried.

“I’m sorry,” Xiaoran mumbled into his jersey.

Yichen let out a breath and rested his chin on top of her head.

“You left your phone.”

“…I know.”

“You disappeared for almost an hour.”

“…I know.”

“You wandered alone without directions.”

“…I KNOW.”

Yichen laughed quietly, mostly out of relief. During the search, he had imagined much worse. Xiaoran was still clinging to him.

“I hate roads,” she declared bitterly.

“That’s not the roads’ fault.”

“Yes it is.”

Yichen pulled back enough to look at her, then paused.

“…Did you buy pastries?”

Xiaoran blinked and looked down at the bags still clutched in her hands. Oh. Right. The original mission.

“They’re for you,” she said weakly.

Yichen stared at her for two seconds. Then he smiled, very softly.

“You got lost while buying me snacks?”

“…Maybe.”

For some reason, that made his expression go even softer.

“You’re unbelievable,” he murmured.

“I almost died.”

“You got mildly misplaced.”

“It was severe.”

Yichen laughed again and took one of the pastry bags from her. Then he laced his fingers through hers and held on tight, like it was automatic.

“You’re not walking anywhere alone anymore,” he decided.

Xiaoran squinted at him.

“You sound like I’m a flight risk.”

“You absolutely are.”

“Rude.”

“You got lost near your own school.”

“…The roads were manipulative.”

Yichen smiled helplessly and led her down the sidewalk. This time, he kept her right beside him the whole way home.

chapters.desc: Insult Lin Xiaoran and she’ll pout. Insult Zhou Yichen in front of her, and you’d better run.
chapters.title: Xiaoran, Don’t Fight
chapters.epigraph: “She couldn’t fight at all. She fought anyway.”
chapters.content:
Very few things could make Lin Xiaoran genuinely violent. Minor inconveniences? She complained loudly. Jealousy? She got petty. Annoyance? She pouted and threatened emotional lawsuits. But an actual fight? Almost never. Mostly because Zhou Yichen usually stepped in before things got that far. But Zhou Yichen wasn’t there that afternoon. And someone insulted him.

✦ ✦ ✦

“Do you think Zhou Yichen will come to the sports festival next week?”

Tang Meilin shifted her shopping bag as they walked down the café street outside school.

“Probably,” Xiaoran said. “He pretends not to care, but he’s secretly dramatic.”

“That’s you.”

“That’s BOTH of us.”

Meilin rolled her eyes fondly. The weather was nice, classes had ended early, and Xiaoran was in an unusually good mood. Until someone called her name.

“Well, if it isn’t Zhou Yichen’s little girlfriend.”

Xiaoran’s smile faded. Standing near the bubble tea shop was Xu Hani. She was dating Song Kai, who captained another school’s basketball team and had been Zhou Yichen’s rival for years. Pretty, arrogant, and very annoying. Beside her, Meilin sighed. Xu Hani crossed her arms, smirking.

“I heard your boyfriend lost his temper during regionals recently.”

Xiaoran stayed calm. Mostly.

“Hm,” she said lazily. “And?”

“Nothing.” Hani shrugged. “Just surprising. Zhou Yichen always acts so perfect.”

Meilin touched Xiaoran’s sleeve. A warning: stay calm. Xiaoran understood.

“I’m not interested in discussing my boyfriend with you,” she said coolly.

A very mature response. Meilin felt proud for about seven seconds. Then Hani laughed.

“I mean, Song Kai says Zhou Yichen only looks scary because people exaggerate him.”

Xiaoran’s expression cooled. Still calm, though. Barely.

“That sounds insecure,” Xiaoran said sweetly.

Hani’s smile stiffened. Inside, Meilin cheered. Good hit. The conversation should have ended there. Instead, Hani stepped closer.

“You know,” she went on, “Song Kai also said Zhou Yichen acts obsessed with basketball because it’s the only thing he’s actually good at.”

Silence. Xiaoran’s fingers tightened around her shopping bag. Still calm. Still ethical. Still surviving. Meilin noticed, though. Danger level rising.

“Hani,” Meilin warned flatly.

But Hani was clearly enjoying herself.

“And honestly,” she added with a mocking laugh, “he’s not even that impressive. Girls just hype him because of his face.”

Xiaoran finally spoke, very quietly.

“Don’t talk about him like that.”

Something in her voice made even Meilin stand up straighter. Hani just rolled her eyes.

“Why?” she scoffed. “Did I hurt your feelings? Your boyfriend isn’t some king.”

Then she made the fatal mistake.

“Honestly,” Hani said with a laugh, “Song Kai could destroy Zhou Yichen anytime if people stopped overrating hi—”

“Don’t.”

Xiaoran cut her off. For one second, everyone went quiet. Lin Xiaoran almost never sounded that cold. Hani blinked, then scoffed again.

“Oh please. You act tough because you hide behind your boyfrie—”

She never finished, because Xiaoran snapped first.

✦ ✦ ✦

Meilin would later describe the fight as “deeply embarrassing for all women involved.” One second they were arguing. The next, there was hair everywhere. Absolute chaos.

“XIAORAN—”

“I TOLD YOU NOT TO TALK ABOUT HIM—”

“ARE YOU INSANE?!”

At some point someone screamed. Someone dropped drinks.

A random auntie nearby shouted, “AIYO!”

Xiaoran had no fighting technique whatsoever. She fought on pure emotion, which somehow made her terrifying. Hani grabbed her hair. Xiaoran grabbed back harder. Shopping bags died in the process.

Meilin tried to pull them apart, yelling, “YOU BOTH LOOK UGLY RIGHT NOW.”

Nobody listened.

By the time some students finally pulled them apart, the damage was done. Hani’s makeup was smeared and her hair was wrecked. Xiaoran stood there breathing hard, a thin scratch across her cheek. And that was exactly when Song Kai and Zhou Yichen arrived—from opposite ends of the street.

✦ ✦ ✦

“XU HANI!”

Song Kai pushed through the crowd first. On the other side, Zhou Yichen stopped dead. Lin Xiaoran looked insane. Hair messy. Breathing hard. Sleeves wrinkled. One tiny scratch across her cheek. And Zhou Yichen’s expression changed. He wasn’t angry first. He was worried first. He was always worried first.

“Xiaoran.”

The second she heard his voice, her anger drained away. Uh oh. Now she remembered consequences existed. Yichen walked quickly toward her while Song Kai rushed to Hani.

“What happened?” Song Kai demanded.

Hani pointed at Xiaoran.

“She attacked me!”

“She insulted Yichen first!” Xiaoran snapped back.

“YOU PULLED MY HAIR.”

“YOU STARTED IT.”

“YOU’RE CRAZY.”

“YOU DESERVED IT.”

“Lin Xiaoran.”

Yichen’s calm voice cut straight through it. Xiaoran froze. She knew that tone. He was serious. Yichen stopped in front of her and gently touched her cheek, just beside the scratch. His jaw tightened.

“…Who scratched you?”

“No one died,” Meilin said quickly, before things could escalate again.

Smart woman. Yichen ignored everyone else, his eyes on Xiaoran’s face.

“You fought?”

Xiaoran suddenly felt guilty.

“…A little.”

Meilin coughed.

“A little? You both turned into wild animals.”

“Traitor.”

Song Kai was staring at the state of Hani in horror.

“What were you even fighting over?”

Hani pointed at Xiaoran again.

“She’s insane about her boyfriend.”

“She insulted him,” Xiaoran said stubbornly.

Song Kai blinked.

“…That’s it?”

“That’s ENOUGH.”

There it was again—that instant protectiveness whenever Zhou Yichen was involved. The crowd was enjoying this far too much. Yichen just looked exhausted. Not embarrassed—exhausted, because Xiaoran had gotten hurt, even a little. He sighed and took her wrist.

“We’re leaving.”

Xiaoran blinked.

“…You’re not angry?”

Yichen looked at her. Then at the scratch again. Then he sighed again.

“I’ll decide after disinfecting your face.”

“Oh.”

Somehow, that was scarier.

✦ ✦ ✦

Ten minutes later, Xiaoran sat on a stool in the pharmacy while Zhou Yichen cleaned the scratch on her cheek. Behind the counter, the pharmacist—an older man in reading glasses—spent a suspiciously long time restocking the cough syrup. She hissed.

“Ow.”

“You fought someone but antiseptic hurts?”

“That’s different emotionally.”

Yichen almost smiled. Almost. Somehow that was worse.

“…Are you disappointed in me?” Xiaoran asked quietly after a while.

Yichen paused, then went back to applying the ointment.

“I don’t like you fighting.”

“…Okay.”

“But.”

Xiaoran looked up. Yichen finally met her eyes.

“What exactly did she say about me?”

Silence. Xiaoran muttered—

“She said people only hype you because of your face.”

Yichen blinked once.

“…That’s the insult?”

“She also said Song Kai could destroy you.”

“Basketball-wise?”

“Yes.”

“And you fought over that?”

Xiaoran looked offended.

“She was disrespectful.”

For a full second, Zhou Yichen honestly didn’t know whether to scold her or laugh. This girl had gotten into a physical fight to defend his reputation. Completely irrational, completely ridiculous, and completely Lin Xiaoran. Finally, he sighed and flicked her forehead.

“You’re unbelievable.”

“Ow.”

“You shouldn’t pull people’s hair.”

“She pulled mine first.”

“You still participated enthusiastically.”

“…That’s true.”

Yichen finally laughed. Relief flooded Xiaoran’s face.

“There,” she whispered. “You’re not mad anymore.”

“I’m still upset.”

“Oh.”

“But mostly,” he admitted, brushing the messy hair away from her face, “I’m just glad you’re okay.”

And just like that, the last of Xiaoran’s anger was gone. There was only warmth left.

chapters.desc: Final exams are coming, Lin Xiaoran just scored 43, and her boyfriend is terrifyingly good at math. What could go wrong?
chapters.title: Lin Xiaoran vs Mathematics (A Tragic Story)
chapters.epigraph: “Some battles are lost before they begin. She fought this one anyway.”
chapters.content:
Lin Xiaoran was naturally good at a lot of things: talking nonsense, being cute, causing emotional stress, and making Zhou Yichen smile without trying. Mathematics was not one of them. In fact, math and Lin Xiaoran had been enemies since childhood.

“Explain this equation to me again,” she demanded, glaring at her workbook like it owed her money.

Across from her, Zhou Yichen stayed painfully calm.

“It’s basic substitution.”

“That sentence means nothing to me.”

“It’s not supposed to.”

Saturday afternoon sun slanted across the library table, which had disappeared under notebooks, snack wrappers, and what was left of Xiaoran’s sanity. Final exams were five weeks away. And after a horrifying 43 on her latest mock test, Lin Xiaoran had finally entered academic crisis.

“I need at least ninety,” she groaned.

Yichen glanced at her paper.

“You need to survive first.”

“Wow.”

“You got three questions wrong before even solving anything.”

“The numbers looked dishonest.”

Yichen sighed. He had expected this the moment she asked him to tutor her. Zhou Yichen was frighteningly good at math. Lin Xiaoran treated formulas like ancient curses. He’d said yes immediately anyway. Severe boyfriend weakness.

“Okay,” he said, pulling her notebook closer. “Focus.”

“I AM focusing.”

“You’ve drawn rabbits in the margin for ten minutes.”

“They help me think.”

“They’re wearing sunglasses.”

“They’re emotionally intelligent rabbits.”

Yichen closed his eyes. It was going to be a long day.

✦ ✦ ✦

At first, Xiaoran genuinely tried. For about twelve minutes. Then disaster struck: Zhou Yichen explaining math was accidentally very attractive.

“Look,” he said, writing neatly across the page, “if x equals three here, substitute it into the equation first, then simplify.”

Xiaoran stared. Not at the equation. At him—his rolled-up sleeves, his calm voice, the small crease that appeared between his brows when he concentrated.

“How are you pretty while solving algebra?” she muttered.

Yichen paused mid-sentence.

“…What?”

“You heard me.”

“I’m teaching.”

“And distracting me on purpose.”

He laughed. Big mistake. Now she was focusing even less. Basketball Yichen was dangerous. Boyfriend Yichen was dangerous. But tutor Yichen, calmly explaining equations in the reading glasses he only wore for studying? Catastrophic.

“Xiaoran.”

“Hm?”

“What did I just explain?”

“…Math.”

Yichen looked at her for a long moment, then took off his glasses.

“That bad?”

“I tried.”

“No, you admired.”

“That too.”

Despite himself, Yichen smiled, which somehow made everything worse.

“This is impossible,” Xiaoran announced, and collapsed face-first onto the table.

“I’m stupid.”

“You’re not stupid.”

“My brain rejected mathematics spiritually.”

“You just have weak fundamentals.”

“That sounds academic and insulting.”

Yichen flicked her forehead.

“Sit properly.”

“No.”

“You wanted tutoring.”

“I wanted emotional support.”

“That’s different.”

“It SHOULD’VE BEEN THE SAME.”

At the next table, a first-year looked up from her textbook, decided she didn’t want to know, and looked back down. Yichen sighed and slid a strawberry milk across the table. Bribery. Effective bribery. Xiaoran sat up at once.

“Fine,” she muttered. “Continue the suffering.”

✦ ✦ ✦

Two hours later, nothing had improved. If anything, it was worse.

“Why is there suddenly a y?” Xiaoran cried.

“Y has been there the entire problem.”

“THEN WHY AM I ONLY SEEING HIM NOW?”

Yichen pinched the bridge of his nose. He had never struggled to teach anyone before. Lin Xiaoran somehow turned math into psychological warfare. At one point, she stared at a formula so long she took it personally. Another time she accused fractions of “looking arrogant.” Right now, she was threatening to fake her own death before exams.

“Focus,” Yichen said, for the fiftieth time.

“I AM.”

“You’re staring out the window.”

“I’m reflecting educationally.”

“No, you’re watching a cat.”

“…The cat understands me.”

Yichen finally laughed into his hand. But Xiaoran was starting to look miserable, sleeves tugged down over her hands, because she really was trying. The numbers just floated around in her head and then disappeared. Watching Yichen solve everything so easily only made it worse.

“You must think I’m dumb,” she mumbled eventually.

Yichen looked up.

“No.”

“But you read something once and just get it.”

“That’s because I studied differently.”

“You’re naturally smart.”

“And you’re naturally good at other things.”

“Like failing?”

“Like making people happy.”

Xiaoran blinked. Yichen continued calmly.

“You remember small details about people. You understand emotions quickly. You make friends easily.” He tapped her notebook lightly. “Math isn’t the only measurement for intelligence.”

Silence. Then Xiaoran slumped against his shoulder.

“…Why are you being nice when I’m trying to spiral?”

“Because I know you.”

He said it simply, like it was obvious, and somehow that made her chest ache more than the homework did. He never made her feel small for struggling. Not even when she got everything wrong. After a moment, Xiaoran muttered—

“…I still want one hundred though.”

Yichen laughed quietly.

“Ambitious.”

“You should support women’s rights.”

“I do.”

“Then help me defeat mathematics.”

He smiled and pulled the workbook back between them.

“Okay,” he said. “One more time.”

She still barely understood algebra. But sitting next to Zhou Yichen, the equations felt a little less terrifying.

chapters.desc: Three weeks of tutoring, one practice test that ends in tears, and a score nobody saw coming.
chapters.title: One Hundred for Love
chapters.epigraph: “Being believed in is its own kind of formula.”
chapters.content:
Three weeks into tutoring, Zhou Yichen learned something important: Lin Xiaoran’s brain ran entirely on emotion. Not logic. Emotion. Which meant normal teaching methods didn’t work.

“Why are you crying over fractions?” Yichen asked one evening.

“Because they’re ugly.”

“That’s not mathematically relevant.”

“It is to ME.”

Xiaoran sat across from him in the library, surrounded by failed worksheets. Yichen was one step away from developing permanent patience issues. Not because Xiaoran was lazy. That was the worst part. She was trying ridiculously hard. She got up early for study sessions. She stayed awake through formulas she didn’t understand. She practiced alone at night, secretly, because she genuinely wanted to get better. But math simply refused to love her back. Today’s practice test: 58. Better than before. Still horrible by Xiaoran’s standards.

“I’m doomed,” she whispered into the table.

“You improved fifteen points.”

“I still look academically illiterate.”

Yichen pulled the worksheet toward him and tapped one section.

“You’re making careless mistakes because you panic.”

“I panic because numbers attack me.”

“They’re not alive.”

“You don’t know their intentions.”

Yichen laughed quietly—then noticed something. Xiaoran wasn’t arguing back. She looked genuinely frustrated, frustrated enough that her eyes had gone a little watery. Oh. Yichen’s expression softened.

“Hey,” he said more gently.

Xiaoran hid her face against the desk.

“I studied really hard.”

“I know.”

“I even memorized formulas.”

“I know.”

“Then why does my brain still stop working during tests?”

Her voice had gone small. That hurt Yichen more than any bad score. Lin Xiaoran rarely took school seriously. But this time, she really wanted that 100. Not because her parents were pushing her, or her teachers. Because once, in passing, Zhou Yichen had said that getting full marks felt satisfying, and now she wanted to know what that felt like too. Dangerously ambitious girlfriend. Operating without mathematical software. Yichen moved his chair next to hers.

“Look at me.”

“No.”

“Xiaoran.”

Slowly, she lifted her head. Her eyes were red-rimmed and her bottom lip was pushed out. Even falling apart, she was cute.

“You know what your problem is?” he asked softly.

“I was born wrong?”

“You stop trusting yourself immediately.”

She blinked.

“You understand more than you think. But the second you see difficult questions, you panic first instead of thinking first.”

“…That sounds psychologically true.”

“It is.”

Xiaoran stared at her worksheet miserably.

“What if I really can’t do it?”

Yichen looked at her for a moment, then smiled a little.

“Then I’ll teach you until you can.”

He said it so simply. It hit harder than she expected. Zhou Yichen never got tired of her. Not when she asked the same question five times, not when she forgot a formula the second he finished explaining it, not even when she wrote a number backwards because she was “emotionally overwhelmed.”

✦ ✦ ✦

They studied every day after that, and slowly, things improved. Not dramatically, not magically, but enough. Yichen started teaching the way her brain worked. Instead of complicated explanations, he made everything about people.

“Think of equations like gossip,” he explained one afternoon.

Xiaoran blinked.

“…What?”

“Numbers affect each other. If one changes, everyone gets involved.”

“…Wait.”

Her eyes went wide.

“…I understand that.”

Yichen looked mildly offended.

“You understand gossip faster than algebra?”

“Yes.”

“Interesting.”

Another day—

“Why do I need this formula?”

“Because the exam likes suffering.”

“Okay, understandable.”

Progress. Actual progress. Even Yuhao was shocked after sitting in on one session.

“She’s improving.”

Yichen nodded calmly.

“She just needs confidence.”

Xiaoran’s eyes were already filling up.

“You believe in me?”

“You literally solved five questions correctly today.”

“OH MY GOD.”

“She’s crying again,” Yuhao observed.

“Leave her alone,” Yichen said, already handing Xiaoran the tissues he’d brought for exactly this reason.

✦ ✦ ✦
