✦ ✦ ✦

Xiaoran looked up at him accusingly.

“…You knew they were abandoning me.”

“Hm.”

“And you allowed it.”

“I’m not seeing the problem.”

So the two of them kept walking through the festival, alone now. And everything felt softer. The evening light turning gold. Music drifting between the booths. Warm air full of food smells and laughter. A comfortable feeling settled between them, like this was a date that had happened without anyone planning it. Then Xiaoran stopped walking. Yichen looked down.

“What happened.”

She pointed.

“Strawberry tanghulu.”

Five minutes later, Xiaoran was happily eating tanghulu while Yichen carried both drinks, because apparently that was his fate in life. Halfway through a strawberry, she froze.

“…Wait.”

“Hm?”

“I ruined your meeting.”

Silence. Yichen knew exactly where this was going. Guilty Lin Xiaoran was stubborn Lin Xiaoran.

“You left your study group because of me.”

“You sounded distressed.”

“That’s not the point.”

“It is to me.”

Xiaoran looked even guiltier.

“I should apologize.”

“No.”

“Yes.”

“Xiaoran.”

“I’m serious.”

Yichen sighed. Once she decided something, especially out of guilt, stopping her was impossible.

✦ ✦ ✦

Twenty minutes later, Lin Xiaoran was standing outside the business faculty study room holding apology drinks for people she had never met. A horrifying experience.

“I can still run away,” she whispered urgently.

Yichen looked calm.

“You dragged me here yourself.”

“I’ve changed my mind.”

“Too late.”

Before she could escape, Yichen opened the door. Several business students looked up, and the room went quiet. So this was THE Lin Xiaoran. The famous girlfriend. The one Zhou Yichen answered calls for during meetings, smiled at his phone for, walked out mid-discussion for. And she looked a lot softer and cuter than they’d expected. Xiaoran nearly died from the staring.

“…Hello.”

One groupmate blinked.

“…Oh.”

Another turned to Yichen.

“You actually brought her here.”

Yichen stayed calm.

“Hm.”

Xiaoran gave a quick little bow.

“I’m sorry for interrupting your meeting earlier.”

Silence. Then she held up the drinks like a peace offering.

“I caused emergency emotionally.”

One groupmate burst out laughing. Another covered his face. Yichen closed his eyes.

“…Emotionally.”

Xiaoran looked defensive.

“That’s what happened.”

The tension broke completely. Then another student grinned.

“So you’re the girlfriend.”

Xiaoran froze.

“…That sounds threatening.”

“No,” the girl laughed immediately. “It’s just funny hearing about you for weeks.”

Xiaoran’s eyes narrowed.

“…Hearing WHAT exactly.”

Yichen sensed danger. Too late. One of the guys answered at once—

“He talks about you constantly.”

Zhou Yichen: “….”

Xiaoran: “…WHAT.”

Another groupmate nodded seriously.

“He leaves exactly at 5 PM because ‘Xiaoran gets hungry around this time.’”

Someone else added—

“And during presentations he checks his phone every ten minutes.”

“And he rejected dinner plans because you had a fever.”

“And he once looked murderous because someone said media students were annoying.”

Xiaoran turned slowly to Yichen, who suddenly looked like he regretted bringing her here at all.

“…Zhou Yichen.”

“Hm.”

“You really are obsessed with me.”

Silence. One groupmate immediately whispered:

“She figured it out.”

Yichen sighed and rubbed between his brows.

“You already knew that.”

“No,” Xiaoran replied seriously. “I knew emotionally.”

A pause.

“Not academically.”

Several business students nearly choked laughing. And for the first time that evening, Yichen actually looked a little embarrassed. Just a little. But Xiaoran noticed, and that made the whole accidental date worth it.

chapters.desc: Zhou Yichen buys a car because of one joke. He is not sorry.
chapters.title: The Day Zhou Yichen Started Looking Expensive
chapters.epigraph: “Some men hold grudges. He held them beautifully.”
chapters.content:
Everyone at university already knew Zhou Yichen came from money. Not in an annoying way. Just obviously. His watches looked expensive. His apartment near campus was suspiciously nice. His calm confidence practically said “raised with financial stability.” But he never acted flashy. Never bragged. Never showed off. Which was exactly why the whole campus nearly lost its mind the day he showed up in a new car.

✦ ✦ ✦

Monday morning, in the business faculty parking lot, half the students stopped walking. Pulling slowly onto campus was a matte black sports car so beautiful it looked unreal. Low engine rumble. Tinted windows. Clean, elegant lines. The kind of car people photographed secretly. Silence spread. Then someone whispered—

“…Whose car is THAT?”

Then the driver’s door opened, and Zhou Yichen stepped out. Black coat. Coffee in one hand. Keys spinning lazily around his fingers. For the first time ever, Zhou Yichen looked rich-rich. Not quietly rich. Not “well-off.” Financially offensive. His business faculty friends looked devastated.

“…You never told us you bought a supercar.”

Yichen shut the car door.

“It’s not a supercar.”

“That thing costs more than my future.”

Another friend narrowed his eyes.

“…Wait.”

“What.”

“You dressed to match the car.”

Silence. Black coat. Black watch. Black car. Oh no. Yichen just sipped his coffee.

“I dressed normally.”

Liar. Terrible liar.

✦ ✦ ✦

It got worse when Lin Xiaoran arrived, because she knew absolutely nothing. At first she only noticed the crowd around the parking lot. Then Luo Jiayi gasped beside her.

“Oh my god there’s a rich man vehicle.”

“University students become very weak around shiny objects,” Xiaoran muttered.

Then someone in the crowd said—

“Isn’t that Zhou Yichen?”

Silence. Xiaoran froze.

“…What.”

The crowd parted a little, and there he was, leaning against the black car, talking to friends, one hand in his coat pocket, morning sun on his profile. Completely calm. Completely handsome. Completely devastating. The car made it so much worse. He looked like a young CEO arriving for a revenge plot. Jiayi grabbed Xiaoran.

“YOUR boyfriend?!”

“I think so.”

“YOU THINK SO?!”

Xiaoran needed several business days to process this. Zhou Yichen looked different today. Not his personality—still calm, still composed, still soft-eyed the moment he noticed her. But there was something unfairly attractive about him standing next to that car. More mature. More intimidating. More… boyfriend-shaped. Then Yichen spotted her, and his expression softened.

“There you are.”

Oh. OH NO. Why did that sound hotter next to an expensive car? Xiaoran walked over weakly.

“…What is this.”

“My car.”

“That’s not a normal sentence.”

Yichen almost smiled.

“I picked it up yesterday.”

“YOU BOUGHT THIS YESTERDAY?!”

Nearby students listened harder. Naturally.

“Hm.”

“Hm?!” Xiaoran stared at him accusingly. “Why are you acting like you bought snacks?”

“It’s just a car.”

“No. This thing has economic influence.”

His friends nearly collapsed laughing. Xiaoran circled the car slowly, like she was investigating dangerous wildlife.

“…You look like a rich villain beside this.”

“That sounds rude.”

“It’s a compliment.”

Then she narrowed her eyes.

“Wait.”

“Hm?”

“…Did you buy this to show off.”

His friends looked very interested. Zhou Yichen never showed off. Ever. So why now? Yichen looked at her calmly for a moment, then answered honestly—

“A little.”

Silence. Everyone froze, Xiaoran included.

“…WHAT.”

A business friend nearly screamed.

“HE ADMITTED IT.”

Yichen looked completely unashamed.

“You said last month that my old car looked too responsible.”

Xiaoran blinked. The memory came back. Oh no. She HAD said that. Specifically—

“You drive like a married businessman with two children.”

And apparently, Zhou Yichen had taken it personally.

“So you bought THIS because of ONE comment?”

“You said I lacked youthful energy.”

“I WAS JOKING.”

“Hm.”

“Oh my god.”

The students nearby were fully invested now. Watching calm, perfect Zhou Yichen buy a luxury sports car because his girlfriend called him boring was insane. Yichen opened the passenger door.

“Get in.”

“…Why.”

“I’ll drive you to class.”

“My building is five minutes away.”

“I know.”

Then Xiaoran understood. He really WAS showing off today. Not arrogantly. Just… specifically for her.

“You’re being very peacock-like today.”

“I learned from media students.”

“That’s discrimination.”

She still got in immediately.

✦ ✦ ✦

The inside was even more terrifying. Soft leather seats. Everything smelled expensive. Xiaoran sat frozen while Yichen drove calmly through campus.

“…You look happy.”

“I’m inside a billionaire dating drama.”

Yichen laughed softly.

“There it is.”

“There WHAT is.”

“You’ve been staring at me weirdly since the parking lot.”

“…Because you suddenly look like a crime.”

“Hm.”

“You’re acting cool on purpose.”

“I’m driving.”

“You know EXACTLY what you’re doing.”

She was right. Every red light was dangerous—one hand resting lazily on the wheel, relaxed posture, quiet confidence. And the worst part was that he wasn’t even trying. Yichen pulled up outside the media building. Before Xiaoran could escape, he leaned a little closer, one arm resting casually behind her seat.

“So.”

Xiaoran’s heart malfunctioned.

“…So what.”

“Do I still look like a married businessman with two children?”

This man held grudges beautifully. Xiaoran looked at him—the expensive car, the calm, handsome face she already liked too much, the boyfriend looking unfairly pleased with himself—and finally, very honestly—

“…No.”

The corner of Yichen’s mouth curved. A tiny victory smile. Xiaoran covered her burning face.

“…You’re unbearable with money.”

That only made Zhou Yichen laugh again.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Lin Xiaoran never does anything quietly.

She complains loudly about tiny inconveniences, gets jealous too easily, cries the moment she’s seriously scolded, and can turn a peaceful afternoon into chaos within minutes. Most people can only handle her in small doses.

Unfortunately for Zhou Yichen, he fell for her almost immediately.

Calm, dependable, and endlessly patient, Yichen spends his days cleaning up after her, buying her strawberry milk before she asks, and pretending he isn’t affected when she hooks her pinky around his sleeve. Their friends think he spoils her too much.

They’re absolutely right.

But even soft love has its hard days. There’s jealousy on both sides, a temper nobody knew Yichen had, a bad landing in a semifinal that leaves Xiaoran more frightened than she has ever been, and one overheard rumor that makes her ask the question neither of them wants to answer: should we break up?

Then comes the future—university applications, a fight about whose dream comes first, results day, graduation, and a new life in Shanghai, where different faculties, new friends, and one very expensive car test whether a high school love can grow up without growing apart.

The story is told in two kinds of chapters. Main chapters follow Xiaoran and Yichen through their relationship in order. Side stories are self-contained moments—birthdays, double dates, terrible poetry, a capybara question—that can be read on their own, in any order.

The Softest Kind of Love is a warm romance about claw machines and borrowed umbrellas, an “I love you” said over shrimp, a first kiss that goes slightly wrong, and two people learning to love each other more gently every day.

contentWarn.content:
This is a gentle romance, but a few chapters include:

• A physical fight between students (Xiaoran, Don’t Fight)

• A sports injury with some blood and a hospital visit (Don’t Scare Me Like That Again, Don’t Limp. I’ll Cry Again.)

• Hurtful rumors and a brief break-up scare (Should We Break Up?)

• Mild language and lots of crying

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
Thank you for spending time with Lin Xiaoran and Zhou Yichen.

This compilation captures the delicate evolution of two teenagers discovering love—not through grand gestures or perfect moments, but through the quiet certainty of choosing each other again and again.

Xiaoran taught me that vulnerability wrapped in humor is still bravery. That crying easily doesn't make you weak; it makes you honest. That love doesn't require perfection; it requires showing up.

Yichen showed me that patience isn't passive. That holding someone's hand matters as much as grand confessions. That the smallest gestures—peeling shrimp, fixing a crooked ribbon, kissing a forehead—can say more than any grand confession.

Their story isn't about fate or destiny.

It's about two people who became each other's home.

One messy, dramatic, beautiful piece at a time.

To everyone who has loved someone who annoys them constantly: your story matters too.

To everyone who has quietly loved without asking for recognition: you are seen.

To everyone building a future with someone else: may you find your middle ground between dreams.
